slots.title: Treasury doubled buybacks; 30-year dip faded in a day
slots.body:
The Treasury doubled its cap on long-end bond buybacks midweek.

The 30-year yield moved down 9 basis points on that news.

By the next day, that entire yield move had reversed.

Reporting on the episode notes Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is scheduled for his first Jackson Hole keynote on Friday, Aug. 28.

Latest Treasury snapshot in the feed (Aug. 20): 10-year at 4.7%, 30-year at 5.2%, 2s10s spread at 0.50.

Prior session equities closed higher anyway:

- S&P 500 +0.4% to 7,674.37
- Dow Jones +1.0% to 53,277.01

What do you watch first when a buyback headline fades in yields but stocks still finish green?
supporting_data: 30-year yield move cited in headline: 9 basis points — [source: Seeking Alpha news]

slots.title: TikTok agrees to $400M U.S. privacy settlement
slots.body:
TikTok agreed to pay $400 million to settle a U.S. DOJ lawsuit over children’s privacy claims, the department announced Friday.

That headline landed the same session U.S. stocks closed up and volatility eased.

Session markers from the feed:

- S&P 500 +0.4% to 7,674.37
- CBOE Volatility Index 15.13 (-5.5%)

Separately, CNBC carried Eurasia Group commentary that the U.S. Treasury’s debt buyback plan is small relative to the overall bond market and that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has limited tools to pull yields lower.

Bitcoin in the cross-asset feed: -1.4% to 77,249.96.

Do you bucket a nine-figure platform settlement with macro weeks like Jackson Hole, or keep regulatory fines in a separate column?

slots.title: Aug. 22 US cash session recap
slots.body:
The Aug. 22 US cash session closed with broad index gains.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished at 53,277.01, up 1.0% (+517.80 points), the strongest move among the major US benchmarks in the feed.
The S&P 500 ended at 7,674.37 (+0.4%, +33.21) and the Nasdaq Composite at 26,180.46 (+0.4%, +113.29).
The Russell 2000 rose 0.9% to 3,017.87.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell 5.5% to 15.13, down 0.88 point from the prior close of 16.01.
That reading sat between the session high of 15.88 and the low of 15.08.

Tesla led megacap percentage moves in the injected data: $TSLA closed at 362.86, up 5.1% (+17.73), with volume near 57.8 million shares and an intraday range of 346.90 to 366.50.

Oracle was the next standout among large caps: $ORCL finished at 146.47, up 3.1% (+4.40), with a high of 147.45.
Salesforce gained 1.8% to 209.17; Microsoft rose 0.4% to 483.24.

Healthcare and consumer names posted solid green closes in the megacap set.
UnitedHealth rose 1.4% to 390.11, Johnson & Johnson 1.1% to 270.24, and Procter & Gamble 1.2% to 144.68.

Payment networks also closed higher: Visa up 1.5% to 371.04 and Mastercard up 1.2% to 580.63.
Broadcom gained 1.2% to 368.45; Taiwan Semiconductor rose 0.7% to 418.95; ASML up 0.8% to 1,763.76.

Several heavily traded megacaps finished lower on the day.
Apple closed at 309.35 (-0.6%), Amazon at 258.63 (-0.6%), Netflix at 79.59 (-0.7%), and NVIDIA at 214.72 (-1.0%).
Exxon Mobil slipped 0.6% to 165.11; Bank of America was down 0.3% to 61.69.
Walmart edged 0.1% lower to 103.70.

Gold futures in the cross-asset block rose 2.4% to 4,680.60 (+109.20), with a session high of 4,690.40.
Brent crude settled at 94.39 (+0.7%); the USO ETF proxy for oil was up 0.1% at 134.64.

Bitcoin USD in the feed printed 77,251.93, up 0.2% (+175.87).
Among active symbols, the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) closed up 6.0% at 43.68 and ProShares Bitcoin ETF (BITO) up 6.1% at 10.41, with heavy volume interest on several crypto-linked actives.

Treasury yield levels in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-08-20) showed the 10-year at 4.7% and the 2s10s spread at 0.50 percentage point.
The dollar proxy UUP was essentially flat at 27.90 (0.0%).

Overseas benchmarks in the same package mixed: Hang Seng rose 2.0% to 26,009.50, FTSE 100 gained 0.6% to 10,816.56, and the Nikkei 225 slipped 0.3% to 66,016.36.

No US economic releases or earnings entries appeared in the injected calendars for this close package; sector ETF performance was not populated in the feed.

slots.title: Core PCE lands Tuesday 12:30 ET
slots.body:
Tuesday Aug. 26, 12:30 p.m.
ET: July inflation and spending data drop in one batch.

Core PCE (prices excluding food and energy, the measure the Fed watches most closely for “underlying” inflation):
- YoY estimate: 3.3% (prior 3.3%)
- MoM estimate: 0.2% (prior 0.1%)

Headline PCE YoY estimate: 3.7% (prior 3.7%).

Same release: Personal Income MoM estimate 0.3% (prior 0.2%).

Same time: Durable Goods Orders MoM estimate +0.7% (prior +0.3%)—factory orders for long-lived items like machinery and aircraft.

The numbers describe what consumers paid and earned in July; they do not tell you what the Fed will do next.

Which line in that stack do you track first—monthly Core PCE or durable goods?

slots.body:
